content: 1. Ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel are indicated for contraception in females of reproductive potential with a BMI less than 30 kg/m², provided a combined hormonal contraceptive is deemed appropriate. However, the drug's effectiveness may be reduced in women with a BMI between 25 and 30 kg/m². 2. The efficacy of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel is expected to remain consistent in postmenarcheal females regardless of age. However, prescribers should consider the reduced effectiveness in women with a BMI between 25 and 30 kg/m². 3. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Co-administration of fezolinetant with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors, including ethinyl estradiol, increases fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and/or dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, with some >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating these hepatitis C combination regimens and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 6. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 8. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 9. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 10. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 11. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease) when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 12. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding may occur. Nonhormonal contraception is advised due to potential fetal harm based on animal studies. 13. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 14. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm, and effective nonhormonal contraception should be used during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 15. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 16. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, including ethinyl estradiol, leading to reduced efficacy. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for females of childbearing potential. 17. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 18. Conivaptan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 19. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 20. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 21. Levonorgestrel transdermal decreases the effects of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during and for one week after elagolix treatment. 22. Elvitegravir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 23. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Encorafenib may cause fetal harm, and effective nonhormonal contraception should be used during treatment and for two weeks after the last dose. 24. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through interactions with OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. Avoid co-administration or adjust substrate dosages as needed. 25. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 26. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 27. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 28. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 29. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib through interactions with CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrates. Avoid co-administration or adjust substrate dosages as needed. 30. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 31. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 32. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 33. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 34. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 35. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 36. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 37. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP substrates. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 38. Lesinurad decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 39. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 40. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 41. Lopinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease) when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 42. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified mechanism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 43. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 44. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone through an unspecified mechanism. Discontinuation of estrogens may be advisable during metyrapone administration. 45. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 46. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 47. Nelfinavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended.
